subject: Discovery recap — Model fit, quantization trade plan & next steps
messages:

Subject: Discovery recap — Model fit, quantization trade plan & next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier, Megan — good to meet you and the FluxFin team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone has the same plan.

Summary of needs (from our call)
- Primary product: real-time risk-scoring assistant for account managers (latency target: p95 < 200ms).
- Throughput: ~750 reqs/min during business hours (bursty).
- Quality: must preserve precision on financial entity extraction and paraphrase detection — <2% regression vs current baseline (human-reviewed).
- Compliance: logs retained for 30 days; PII redaction required in outputs.

Recommended candidate models (first pass)
- Llama-3-70B-instruct — best baseline for instruction-following at longer context (~8k tokens). Good for paraphrase/analysis quality.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (multi-turn tuned) — strong latency/cost profile for shorter prompts and synthesis tasks.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (quant-aware) — intermediate option, sometimes balances latency and accuracy for tabular-to-text translations.

Benchmarks & artifacts I attached
- redwood-reference-bench-20270522.xlsx (sanitized throughput / latency estimates across FP16, AWQ-4, GPTQ-4, and FP8-ish configs).
- fluxfin-sample-prompts.csv (what you shared; we sanitized for our bench).
- Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-ref-benchmarks-2027

Quantization / throughput trade summary (high level)
- AWQ (4-bit): usually offers the biggest cost/throughput win vs FP16 and often preserves instruction-following quality on Llama-family models, but can show narrow regressions on entity extraction and numeric fidelity without calibration.
- GPTQ (4-bit): more deterministic on some model families (e.g., Falcon) but requires careful per-layer treatment; higher engineering effort to automate without rollbacks.
- FP8 / mixed 8-bit: promising for throughput while keeping fidelity, but hardware support still uneven depending on infra — this is good for Dedicated/Private deployments with consistent HW.

Immediate asks / proposed experiments (mutual action plan)
1) FluxFin to confirm access to a representative set of ~250 labeled examples (entity + paraphrase labels) and the sample production prompts referenced in the sheet. (You indicated this is doable.)
2) Redwood will run a 3-stage eval: baseline FP16 (A0), AWQ-4 (A1), GPTQ-4 (A2) on the top two candidate models. Aim: measure p95 latency, token cost, and label-level regression (precision/recall).
3) If we see >2% quality regression on A1/A2, run mitigation: prompt engineering + small LoRA (2-4M params) and re-evaluate.

Proposed timeline
- Week 0 (this week): get sample data + access; agree on eval metric definitions.
- Week 1: Redwood runs bench + quality evals; quick summary + suggested model/config.
- Week 2: Technical deep-dive with engineering (we can include a brief demo of Dedicated routing).

Next steps for scheduling
- Can you confirm a good time for the Week 2 deep-dive (prefer Thurs/Fri next week)?
- Confirm a dropbox/secure link for the labeled 250 examples.

Thanks — looping in Lauren (quant lead) and Ben (solutions) to align on the experiment matrix.

—

Thanks Megan / Connor — short technical note to set expectations on the quant matrix.

Our recommended experiment matrix (short)
- A0: FP16 baseline (Llama-3-70B, Mistral-7B) — measure latency, tokens/sec, and label F1.
- A1: AWQ-4 (Llama-3-70B, if available) — typically "drop" risk: small precision hits on numeric extraction; good throughput gains (~2.5–3x token throughput in our infra).
- A2: GPTQ-4 (Falcon family or Llama variants) — often more stable on Falcon-like architectures; throughput gain similar to AWQ but with higher conversion time and occasionally higher variance.
- A3: FP8 mixed (where hardware supports) — target for Dedicated; expect ~1.8–2.2x throughput with near-FP16 fidelity on many tasks.

Notes on measurement and thresholding
- Primary metric: label-level F1 on your sanitized entity/paraphrase set. Secondary: p95 latency (ms) end-to-end.
- Pass condition: relative F1 drop <= 2% vs A0; if >2% we apply mitigations (prompt templates + small LoRA fine-tune).

Mitigation playbook (if regression observed)
1) Prompt engineering (short canonical templates) — usually low effort and effective for paraphrase/formatting regressions.
2) Small LoRA adaptation (1–4M params) on labeled examples — reduces regressions for numeric/entity tasks with modest cost.
3) Model variant fallback policy in production: burst route to FP16 or smaller model if AWQ/GPTQ result fails checks.

Attachment: quant-experiment-matrix.md (detailed steps and expected infra costs).

I'll kick off a small internal job to run AWQ/GPTQ converts once we have your sample and confirm which models you want prioritized.

—
Lauren Bishop
